notes: Small-scale, LOW-REYNOLDS rotor: chord Reynolds number ~3e4 (tsr 3) to ~1e5 (tsr 10); at the Cp peak ~6e4-9e4 over the outer blade. Polars are given only for Re 47k-84k, so the low-tsr points use extrapolated Re. Geometry = TUM's own AeroDyn 60-node blade table (R = TipRad 0.5495 m, hub 0.0535 m); the data providers normalise Cp/Ct/TSR with D = 1.1 m (R = 0.55 m): the area differs by 0.18 %, which is negligible. Twist is already in the solver convention (OpenFAST BlTwist, no pitch); global pitch 0.4 deg is in the experiment defaults. Root: cylinder (cd = 1.0 per TUM) to r = 0.07 m, transition to RG14 by r ~ 0.13 m with TUM's own transition polars (sections 2-9); transition coordinates are generated (circle/RG14 blends matching the design t/c) and only matter for structural properties. TUM polar files have cm identical to cl (file error) - cm dropped. BLOCKAGE: the TUM-tunnel data (20 % blockage, uncorrected) give Cp,max = 0.505 at tsr ~8.3, whereas the same rotor gives ~0.42 in the larger PoliMi tunnel (Campagnolo et al. 2016, Nanos et al. 2022) and 0.39 at tsr 8.4 in the NTUA tunnel (11 % blockage; file performance_ntua_upstream_turbine_point.csv). An unbounded-flow BEM should therefore UNDER-predict the TUM Cp/Ct; apply a blockage correction (e.g. Glauert / Bahaj et al. 2007, tunnel area 2.7 x 1.8 = 4.86 m^2) or compare trends only. The polars were tuned (identified) from G1 rotor measurements in the PoliMi tunnel, so agreement near the design point partly reflects that calibration; the stall side (tsr < 6) and the high-tsr side are the more independent test. Inflow is a low-turbulence boundary-layer profile; hub height 0.82 m. Thrust is from the tower-base load cell with the nacelle/tower drag contribution as handled by the providers (not stated).
